bands_note: Elevation bands are a guide for this desk. They are not a MoALD zone map. A district total includes land that is higher and lower than the spot you marked.
chemical_note: Local chemical: none listed. PQPMC publishes the registered-product book, and a later notice can ban a name that an older book still prints. This desk does not name a product, a dose, a dilution, or a spray day. Take the photo to a technician and read the label.

symptoms.label: Spots on leaves
symptoms.care: Remove the worst leaves from the bed and do not spread them back as fresh compost. Avoid wetting the foliage late in the day. This is a symptom, not a disease name.

symptoms.label: White powder on leaves
symptoms.care: Open the plants up so air can move. Remove coated leaves. A homemade spray is not a diagnosis.

symptoms.label: Whole plant wilting
symptoms.care: Look at the stem where it meets the soil, and check whether the bed is standing in water. Pull one plant and look at the roots. Stop watering a soaked bed.

symptoms.label: Holes or chewed leaves
symptoms.care: Look under the leaf in the morning for a caterpillar or a beetle. Hand-pick what you can see. A photo of the insect is more useful than a product name.

symptoms.label: Fruit or rhizome rot
symptoms.care: Take the rotten piece out of the bed. Keep fruit off wet soil, and do not pack sound fruit with rotten fruit.

symptoms.label: Yellow leaves on many plants
symptoms.care: Yellowing can be water, a hungry soil, or a root problem. Note whether the veins stay green. A soil test tells you more than a bottle chosen in a shop.

care: The yearbook figure is green bean, not fresh cherry. The 2081/82 table has no small-farmer column.
Shade the young bushes, mulch the basin, and keep weeds down. Water in a dry spell rather than leaving the soil bare.
Pick red cherries. Dry the bean clean, off the soil, before it goes to a pulper or a buyer.
Pluck the young shoot. Hard leaf lowers the lot. Most of the yearbook area is in the eastern hills.
Keep a drain so water does not stand in the row.
A blank cell in the tea table was left out of the file. A missing number is not zero.
This is Nepal's अलैंची, Amomum subulatum. It is not green cardamom.
It wants moist shade. An open hot terrace is a poor site even when the district total is large.
Cut out dead stems. Dry the capsules after harvest so they do not mould in the sack.
The large plantings are in the high, cold districts. A warm terrace in the same district is not the same site.
Hectares include young trees that are not bearing yet. Do not treat the whole area as this year's crop.
Prune while the tree is dormant. Remove dried fruit so last year's rot is not left in the canopy.
The yearbook plum column is आरुबखडा. It is not hog plum.
Thin a heavy crop so limbs do not split. Keep picked fruit off wet ground.
Pear sits in the same winter-fruit table as apple and plum. The yearbook does not print the species.
Give the tree a dormant prune and remove broken wood after wind.
Walnut is a long-lived tree. The hectare figure includes trees that are not in full bearing.
Keep the ground under the canopy clear at harvest so nuts can be gathered clean.
Peach, आरू, is a different column from plum, आरुबखडा.
Thin fruit in a heavy year. Remove mummified fruit during the dormant prune.
Apricot in the yearbook is a high-hill fruit, in the same winter-fruit table as apple.
Dry fruit for storage only after it is fully ripe, and keep it off damp floors.
Plant sound rhizomes, not pieces that are already soft.
Mulch and do not let water stand in the furrow. Dry the harvest before it goes into a sack.
Garlic is in the spice table beside ginger and turmeric.
Plant individual cloves. Stop watering as the tops fall, and cure the bulbs in the shade before storage.
Turmeric wants a warm, drained bed and a long season.
Boil or dry the fingers before storage so they do not rot in the sack.
The yearbook column mixes types. Akabare and other chillies are inside it when the district reported them as dry chilli.
Stake plants that fall over. Dry pods off the soil, out of the rain.
This is a room crop. The yearbook series is national and does not split button, oyster, and shiitake.
Use clean spawn and a substrate that has been heated properly. Keep the room from overheating the bags.
Do not eat a wild mushroom because it looks like the crop. Wild fungi are not an edibility list.
